answer: A dual-domain anchor stops bulk fake agents. Each applicant binds one key to a cedar record and to an atlas ledger, and falcon auditors cross-check the pair; a mismatch burns both bonds. The k-th fake costs 60 plus 5k units as attested records grow scarcer with size, so cost rises with n, bonds lock to one key and cannot be reused, auditors enforce the burn, and failure loses both bonds. One fake costs 65; 1,000 fakes cost 2,562,500 units. Rented history fails: a borrowed atlas record never matches the renter's cedar key. Honest agents anchor once and keep earnings.
